//: The bake demo's material (ADR 0045): the same shape as pbr_cube's
noise work, but over the *uv* — because a bake's domain is the uv.
The cone that computes `roughness` — surface uv, split, a 3D domain
built from it, twelve octaves of fbm, a remap — is declared baked:
`bakes` names the node whose value becomes a 256x256 table, and the
material then either samples that table (one texture read) or
evaluates the whole cone per fragment (the toggle,
MaterialConfig::bakes, and the point of the item: the two arms draw
the same picture and cost different amounts). The declaration is a
claim about node 5 — bake *this* — not a node of its own, so the
graph reads exactly as it would unbaked.
Purity is the one authoring rule: the baked cone may read `input.uv`
(that is the domain) and nothing else — no world position, no time, no
parameters, no textures. A bake is a pure function of where it is
sampled; that is what makes sampling it back equal computing it.
The cone also belongs to the bake alone: nothing else may read the
nodes feeding the remap, or they would go dark when the bake is on.
WXSL_FBM_OCTAVES is pinned here rather than in the material config
so both arms of the toggle compile the same loop — the bake module
and the inline material must agree about what they compute.
name: bake term
